title: KV-shadowing: quantized KV shadow caching for amortized dequant during prefill/decode
creator: Marcos Rivera
description: Problem: dequantizing KV cache during streaming prefill and decode adds measurable per-request overhead on mixed-precision paths (INT8/FP8). Goal: introduce a low-overhead 'shadow' cache that stores compact quantized KV representations aligned to the runtime's kernel formats to avoid repeated dequant/requant cycles across microbatches and model rollouts. This reduces per-token CPU/GPU overhead, improves end-to-end decode latency for short sequences, and reduces host<->device transfer waste for multi-tenant Dedicated nodes. Scope: design and implement a runtime-level cache layer plus kernel adapters and fallbacks for incompatible shapes/versions. Not in scope: user-facing API changes and offline model quantization tooling.
technical_spec:
High-level approach:
1) Shadow KV store: persistent per-session store that keeps the most recent KV tensors in their compact quantized layout (INT8 or FP8 depending on backend). Each shadow entry includes: format_tag, per-head scales/zero-points (where applicable), sequence_range, and a small version tag. Entries are keyed by (session_id, layer_index, head_block, seq_start).
2) Kernel adapters: extend kernel selection to accept shadow entries directly, enabling kernels to consume quantized KV without host-side dequant. For kernels requiring FP32 accumulation, provide in-kernel dequant that operates fused with attention compute to avoid separate temp buffers.
3) Amortized dequant policy: introduce heuristics to decide when to keep quantized shadow vs materialize full FP KV (e.g., when many small microbatches reuse same prefix). Policy signals: reuse_count, average_microbatch_length, downstream model variant compatibility.
4) Consistency and rollouts: version tag used to invalidate shadow entries when model weights or quantization parameters change. Rollout path: fallback to existing dequant flow on mismatch.
5) Telemetry and tuning: expose metrics for reuse_rate, avg_dequant_time_saved, memory_delta, and kernel_fallback_rate. Use these to train a lightweight cost model that tunes keep/drop thresholds per deployment tier.
Design trade-offs:
- Storing quantized shadow reduces memory compared to full FP materialization but needs additional per-entry metadata.
- In-kernel fused dequant reduces host overhead but increases kernel complexity and maintenance burden across hardware vendors.
- Heuristic policies risk keeping stale shadows; conservative defaults with fast invalidation are chosen for safety.
Compatibility considerations:
- Backend adapters for NVIDIA and AMD providers required; for unsupported backends the runtime falls back to existing dequant path.
- Works with both static per-layer quantization and per-channel scales; we require per-head scale metadata for attention heads to enable correct accumulation.
Performance targets:
- Reduce average per-request dequant CPU time by >= 60% on short-sequence (<=64 tokens) workloads.
- Reduce tail (95p) decode latency by >=10% for chat-like traffic on Dedicated nodes.
- Net GPU memory change <= +5% for default keep policy.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes shadow KV store and can populate entries during prefill without changing API surface.
Kernel selection can consume shadow entries; at least one fused quant-consume attention kernel implemented and validated on NVIDIA A100 (CUDA) path.
Benchmarks show >=60% reduction in host dequant time for short sequences and >=10% 95p latency improvement on representative chat workload.
Shadow invalidation works correctly across model rollouts and when quantization meta changes (automated tests included).
Feature guarded behind a runtime flag and off by default for private deployments until validated in Dedicated canary.
implementation_notes: Spike: microbench shadow entry layout and serialization format (Mar 17–21) - prototyped in runtime/shadow_kv/ (internal branch).
Kernel work: add fused quant-consume attention kernel (runtime/kernels/quant_consume_attn.cu). Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
Runtime: integrate shadow lifecycle in prefill path and session GC (runtime/session_cache.cpp). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1435
Telemetry: dashboard tile for shadow reuse (Console dashboard ref: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/runtime/shadow-kv) and PerfDash comparisons attached.
Unit tests for versioned invalidation and fallback (tests/shadow_kv_test.cpp).
Rollout plan: behind runtime-flag --shadow-kv; enable first on internal canary Dedicated pool, then beta customers, then GA after two weeks of steady telemetry.
